maren-job.title: Maren's Job
text: Maren has a lake chart spread on the council table, weighted at the corners with a whetstone and three cold cups. Her finger rests on the island nobody visits. "Fishermen see a light out there on calm nights. Low, by the water. And something big has started coming into the Shallows after dark. I want to know who lands on that island, and what moves in the water. Take a boat. Come back."
Maren is Captain of The Fort. She was an imperial soldier once. She still stands like one.

choices.text: Ask about the pay.
say: "Twenty gold each from the common chest, when you report. And first pick of anything that isn't The Fort's." She pushes a purse across the table. "Twenty now, for oil and rope."

choices.text: Ask what she is not saying.
say: "Since the Gorgon Queen fell, someone has been buying every cockatrice egg Harrow can find. I think that someone uses the island. I want proof before I accuse a man I need."

choices.text: Ask about the Gorgon Queen.
say: "A cockatrice chick's cry paralysed her. Biddy's cry. Wick keeps her now. Everyone keeps clear of her beak, and everyone on the lake has heard of her. That is why the eggs sell high."

choices.text: Ask about the boat.
say: "One of the two rowboats. It holds four with gear. The sailboat, if I trust you." She looks at you. "I will see."

choices.text: Take the twenty gold.
say: Twenty gold, in a leather purse. It is not much.

choices.text: Take the job.
say: Planning is free. Execution costs time, and the lake does not wait.

maren-report.title: Report to Maren
text: Maren has the common chest open on the council table. "Tell me what you saw. Not what you think. What you saw."

choices.text: Tell her who lands on the island.
say: "Smugglers. Coast folk in oilskins crusted white with salt. They tar their ropes. They chalk an eye with a line through it." Maren counts out forty gold.

choices.text: Tell her what moves in the water.
say: "A fish. A giant catfish in a bronze collar." Maren says nothing for a while. Then she counts out forty gold.

choices.text: Put the ledger on the table.
say: Maren reads it twice. Then she puts it in her coat and goes to find Harrow. "Wait here," she says. You do not.

choices.text: That is all.
say: "Then rest. You have earned it."

rumors.title: A Drink at the Hall
text: Buy a drink and listen. Some of it is true.

choices.text: A fisher, low.
say: "There's a boat out there with no lamp. It comes and goes from the isle on still nights. Not ours. Not from the village."

choices.text: An old soldier.
say: "The tower was a lighthouse for the old empire's lake fleet."

choices.text: A net-mender.
say: "Something big lives off the isle. It took a net and the boy holding it, my grandfather's time."

choices.text: A child, bold.
say: "The keeper out there was a wizard. Turned his servants to bone so they'd work forever."

choices.text: A drunk.
say: "There's a sunken treasure ship under the jetty."

choices.text: A farmer's wife.
say: "Chalk eyes on a door mean a curse. Don't go through."

choices.text: Someone at the back.
say: "Harrow's buying cockatrice eggs at double since Biddy's cry froze the Gorgon Queen. Says a cockatrice is worth ten swords now."

choices.text: A boatwright.
say: "The cellars under the tower go out under the lake, all the way to the Deep."

choices.text: A girl on the wall.
say: "The old stones on the isle's shore hum before a storm. Put your ear to one and you'll hear your name."

choices.text: Wick, counting.
say: "The Quiet on the Reed Shore know the isle. Bring them salt, not silver."

choices.text: That is enough.
say: You put the cup down.

cassandra.title: Cassandra
text: Cassandra sits by the shrine door with her hands in her sleeves. She tells true things, half of them in riddles. She answers a question with a question. She gives one hint a visit.

choices.text: Ask about the water.
say: "What turns a stair into a door? And who holds the wheel?"

choices.text: Ask about the fish.
say: "A servant remembers its master's face. What colour is a keeper's face?"

choices.text: Ask about the dead.
say: "The keeper asked for words, and nobody came. Who has read his last page?"

choices.text: Ask about the shore stones.
say: "Eight stones, and a dish on each. What does a lit dish call?"

choices.text: Ask about the Saltmen.
say: "Salt walks where silver is refused. What does the eye with a line through it say, to those who can read it?"

choices.text: Ask nothing.
say: She nods, as if you had.

crossing.title: The Crossing
text: Twelve miles of lake, north from The Fort's docks across the Shallows. Fish by day. Singing at night.

Four to five hours by rowboat. Leave at dawn and you land at midday, with a full afternoon on the isle. Leave at midday and you land near dusk, and the Warden circles the isle at dusk. Coming home takes as long.

choices.text: Ask about the Shallows.
say: By day the water is clear to the weed and full of perch. By night it sings: a low chord under the hull, felt in the oar-handles more than heard. Anyone who trails a hand in it hears words in no language.

choices.text: Ask about the Reed Shore.
say: Stilt huts in the reeds on the lake's east side, an hour's detour. The people there are called the Quiet. They do not speak aloud. They answer with hands and knotted cords.

choices.text: Row straight for the isle. Land by day.

say: You row north. The Fort shrinks to a smudge of smoke. The water goes shallow and green, then deep and grey, then shallow again.

choices.text: Put in at the Reed Shore first. Land at dusk.
Not yet.
say: The boats knock at the pilings.

reed-shore.title: The Reed Shore
text: A woman of the Quiet sits on a hut ladder, mending a net. She does not speak. Nobody here speaks to strangers.
Behind her, cords hang from the hut rails. Each is knotted differently.

choices.text: Ask about the isle.
say: She draws a circle in the mud. She puts eight stones round it. She puts one large fish inside. Then she wipes it all out, except the fish.

choices.text: Ask about the boat with no lights.
say: She ties a cord with four knots and a gap. Four nights. The last run.

choices.text: Ask for a guide.
say: She holds out both hands, palms up. Salt. One of the Quiet will come for a gift of salt. A guide points the safe landing, refuses to set foot past the jetty, and waits in the boat.

choices.text: Give them salt.

say: She takes it with both hands. Salt is worth more to them than coin. A boy climbs into your boat without a word.

choices.text: Turn back to The Fort.
Row on to the isle as the light goes.

say: You row the last miles with the sun behind the trees. Behind you, the Shallows begin to sing.

dark.title: Dark
text: The last light goes out. There is no flame in the pack, and no flask in the lantern. The dark is complete. The walls are somewhere.

choices.text: Stand still and think.
say: Torches burn six turns. A flask in a lantern burns twenty-four. A light spell, if one of you has it, burns twelve. Use it, or go home.

choices.text: Feel your way back to the Fort. Hand on the wall, all the way.

s1.title: The Broken Jetty
text: The jetty is old dressed stone, black with weed to the tideless waterline, and its far end has slumped into the lake like a tired arm. A post of grey oak stands where it meets the shore. Its iron ring is bright where a rope has lately worn it. Past the broken end the water lifts in one long, smooth swell, as if something the size of your boat turned over in its sleep; then the lake is flat again.
The jetty is ten feet wide, so two can stand side by side.
notes: What this room teaches. Planning, then Execution. Looking and asking are free. Acting costs a turn. Set your marching order and your light now.

choices.text: Look at the mooring post.
say: The rope burn is fresh: days, not weeks. Tar fibres in the ring. The Saltmen tar their ropes. Someone else lands here when the north side is rough.

choices.text: Look at the bootprints on the path north.
say: Heavy boots, several men. A week old under fresh needles. They lead toward the tower.

choices.text: Look at the stone along the shore.
say: Ten yards along the shore stands a man-high stone with a carved eye and a bronze dish on top. One of eight. There are more on the east point.

choices.text: Ask the Minister what she saw in the water.
say: "A long back, wet and dark. There was a gleam on it. Metal, I think." Her hand is on her holy symbol. She says no more.

choices.text: Watch the water for a full turn.

say: The swell comes round the east point and goes west. It circles the isle, clockwise, and it leaves the south water empty for a time.

choices.text: I've Read About This: name the thing in the water.

say: You say it plainly. A bound guard of the old station, in a bronze collar. It does not hunt. It keeps its post.
The Minister, softly: "The Terminal remembers."

choices.text: The Land Speaks: put your palm on the island.

say: Under your palm the island is full of small hungry lives. Rats. Many, and starving, in the dark under the tower. You count as having heard them.

s2.title: The Tower Shell
text: The tower is a drum of grey stone with the sky for a lid. Its upper floors lie on the ground floor in a hill of masonry, beams and green glass. A stair, each step a stone tongue set in the wall, climbs round the inside to a broken lip forty feet up, where crows sit and comment on you. Over the door, letters cut deep and filled with old verdigris.
notes: Size: round, 30' across inside. Walls 4' thick.
What this room teaches. Searching costs time. Finding the trapdoor is one turn. Climbing for the view is another. The nest is a third. You can have all three, but the clock moves.

choices.text: Read the letters over the door.
say: Imperial Common, cut deep, filled with verdigris: STATION NINE. KEEP THE LIGHT. KEEP THE DOOR.
The Elf Minister and the Paladin read it at once. Others with INT 13 or more puzzle it out in a turn.

choices.text: Look at the green glass.
say: Shards of the great lens, thick as a thumb. The station's light was green.

choices.text: Ask the Minister about the crows.
say: "Crows nest where nobody comes. Somebody comes here. Look how they hate the light."

choices.text: I Remember When: you have stood in this tower.

say: There was a trapdoor in the floor, once, in the north-west corner under the slates. You say where. No search is needed.

choices.text: Speak with Animals: ask the crows who comes here.

say: A crow drops onto the rail and tells it the crow way: men come by boat to the north cliff, and leave the boat under the overhang. No lamp.

choices.text: Search the rubble. One turn.

say: You shift slates and rotten beams for ten minutes. In the north-west corner: iron-bound oak, a ring handle, four feet square. Cold air breathes out of it. It smells of lamp oil and wet stone.

choices.text: Climb the stair for the view. One turn.
Lift the trapdoor and go down. One turn.

s2-search.title: Rubble
text: You work through the rubble, square by square. Under the slates and beams, in the north-west corner of the floor: iron-bound oak, a ring handle, four feet square. Cold air breathes out of it. It smells of lamp oil and wet stone.

choices.text: Lift the trapdoor and go down. One turn.
Mark the trapdoor on your map, then leave.
say: Marked. You can walk into it from the corner.

s2-top.title: The Stair Top
text: The stair is narrow and the crows do not like you. At the top the wall ends in broken teeth, forty feet up. The crows mob whoever climbs. That is noise.
You can see the whole isle: the jetty, the cottage at the tower's foot, the lamp-stones on the east point. At the north cliff, under the overhang, a boat-shaped shadow lies in the water.

choices.text: Look at the north cliff.
say: Under the overhang, a shadow the length of a boat. No lamp. No one aboard that you can see. Whoever lands here hides the boat where The Fort's watch cannot see it.

choices.text: Count the lamp-stones along the shore.
say: Three on the east point. Five more alone round the shore. Eight, in a ring.

choices.text: Search the crows' nest. One turn.

say: In the nest: a silver ring stamped with a lamp and the numeral IX.

choices.text: Climb down. One turn.

s3.title: The Keeper's Cottage
text: A keeper's cottage, stone to the shoulder and open to the weather above. Someone has slept here lately: the hearth holds a grey drift of ash with no rain in it, and fish bones picked clean. On the door, in fresh chalk, an eye has been drawn and struck through with one hard line.
notes: What this room teaches. Searching costs time, and you choose where. Six squares, six turns to search it all. The oil and salt are in plain view, free. The bed is a turn spent for nothing.

choices.text: Look at the chalk mark on the door.
say: An eye with a line through it. The Minister knows it: "Chalked on a crate in Old Harrow's cart. I thought it was a tally." It is not a tally. It is a Saltmen sign, and it means: keep out. It appears again in the cellars.

choices.text: Look at the hearth.
say: Ash less than a week old. A broken clay pipe of coast make. Fish bones, picked clean. This is the only square in the room someone has used.

choices.text: Take the tin of lamp oil from the shelf.
say: A tin of lamp oil, two flasks' worth. In plain view, so it costs nothing.

choices.text: Take the dish of coarse salt.
say: A stone dish of coarse salt. It strips leeches off a wader without harm.

choices.text: Search the hearth. One turn.

say: A loose hearthstone. Under it, an iron key. It will open the locked door in the cellars.

choices.text: Search the bed frame. One turn.

say: Rotted rope. Under it, nothing. A turn spent for nothing is allowed.

s3-search.title: Searching the Cottage
text: Ten minutes of kicking at pine needles. You find nothing yet.
notes: Six squares, six turns to search it all. Ask where someone has been.

s4.title: The Lamp-Stones
text: Three standing stones lean together on the point like old men at a rail. Each bears one carved eye at the height of your own, and each wears a bronze dish on its head, crusted green and full of rain. Up close they hum, low, as a hive hums in winter. The hum is in your teeth before it is in your ears.
notes: What this room teaches. The isle is one machine. The stones on the shore, the eyes in the cellars and the collar on the fish are parts of one thing. Reading the site starts on the surface.

choices.text: Put your ear to a stone.
say: The hum is louder at dawn and dusk. The Paladin feels it as the wards' pulse. The Druid hears the same note as the Shallows. It does not say names.

choices.text: Look at the carved eyes.
say: The same carving as in the Gorgon Queen's chamber. Anyone who was there knows it on sight.

choices.text: Look at the fallen stone on the south shore.
say: One of the five lone stones lies broken. Bronze wire runs out of the break and into the rock. The stones are posts in a fence, and the fence is wired.

choices.text: Count the stones.
say: Eight in all, in a ring round the shore. The Warden cannot pass outside them.

choices.text: Pour a flask of oil into a dish and light it. One turn.

say: The stone's eye glows green. A swell turns in the water offshore and comes to that stone, and circles there. It is leaving the pool empty while it does.
It will not last. Six turns, no more.

choices.text: The Oath Remembers: these are wards.

say: The stones are wards. So is the ring in the cellars. Keeping them lit is in the oath. The knights of the order once relieved this post.

choices.text: The Land Speaks: the ground in a ring.

say: The bronze wire runs through the rock. The ground in a ring round the isle is dead an inch down. The sickness is a collar, and it is worn by a fish.

s5.title: The North Cliff
text: The pines stop and the isle ends in a drop of grey rock to dark water. Below, the cliff foot is hollowed into a cave mouth, and in its throat a long open boat rides at a line, a man in an oilskin sitting in the stern with a rod. A cleft splits the cliff top beside you; a tarred rope, knotted every foot, is tied off to a pine root and drops into it.
notes: What this room teaches. There is more than one way in. The rope reaches the grotto without passing a single cellar. It is the fast road to the climax and the worst one: it lands you at the Saltmen's front door, unprepared.

choices.text: Look at the boat.
say: Thirty feet, oars, a lug sail. The boat-shaped shadow seen from the tower. The Saltmen's only way off the isle.

choices.text: Look at the rope.
say: Tarred, knotted every foot, tied off to a pine root. Fifty feet down to the ledge in the cave. In plate armour the climb takes two turns.

choices.text: Look at the ground by the cleft.
say: Bootprints, worn deep between the cleft and the cottage. A week of men going back and forth.

choices.text: Lie still at the edge and watch. One turn.

say: The man in the boat looks up. He sees the edge of a face. He does not shout, yet.
He ships his rod. He rings a small hand bell, twice, before he takes the oars. The bell matters here.

choices.text: To go down, walk into the cleft.
say: The rope is the stair here. Climbing down takes one turn and needs no roll.

c1-search.title: Searching the Landing
text: Ten minutes at the stones of the landing, every one you can reach.
notes: Searching is a roll, not a certainty: 1 in 6, and elves 2 in 6. A miss does not mean nothing is there. A hit shows in the log.

c1.title: The Cellar Stair
text: The stair goes down into a cold that has been waiting a long time. Every ten feet an iron hook juts from the wall for a lamp that is no longer there. At the bottom, on a landing hardly bigger than a cupboard, an oak door stands shut, black with age and swollen in its frame.
notes: Size: stair 10' wide, 30' long, falling 20'. A 10' landing at the bottom. The oak door at the bottom is stuck.
Listening: 1 in 6; demi-humans 2 in 6. Forcing: 1 or 2 on a d6, and STR adds. Each try is loud: the clock rolls, and the rats are not surprised.
What this room teaches. Listening and doors. Listen first, then force. Each try is a noise, and noise brings the clock.

choices.text: Look at the oak door.
say: Black with age and swollen in its frame. Along the bottom edge: scratches, made from the other side.

choices.text: Look at the lamp hooks.
say: Bronze, worth nothing. Each one is stamped IX.

choices.text: Look at the walls of the landing.
say: Close stone, ten feet apart. The east wall is cold to the touch and a little too clean. Searching the landing takes a turn.

choices.text: Listen at the door. No time passes.

say: Scratching. Squeaks. Many small claws on stone.
You hear nothing. That is not the same as nothing being there.

choices.text: I Know How This Was Made: look at how the door was hung.

say: You lift, you shoulder, and the leaf comes up off its pins and swings in without a sound. Behind you it drops back into its frame and sticks.

c2.title: The Oil Store
text: Racks of clay oil jars line the walls, most of them broken, and the floor is a black skin of old spill that takes your bootprints like wax. The air is thick with the smell of it. Something heavy and many-footed scatters from your light into the racks, and then the squeaking starts.
notes: Giant rats, five. AC 7 [12], bite 1d3, speed 120' (40'), swim 60' (20'), morale 8. They flee at 2 dead.
If you heard them at the door, you strike first. If not, they bite first.
What this room teaches. The clock is a monster. Every 2 turns it rolls a die: 1 in 6, and something comes.
Five at once. If a round goes badly, choose Run.

choices.text: Look at the floor.
say: Old oil, gummy and slow. It will not catch from a dropped torch. A fresh flask poured on it and lit would burn.

choices.text: Look at the far corner.
say: Shredded sacking and bones. Nothing of value.

choices.text: Look along the racks.
say: Most jars are smashed and their oil long gone into the floor.

choices.text: Fight the rats.
Back out through the doorway to the landing.

c2-after.title: The Oil Store, After
text: The squeaking is gone. The dead lie on the oily floor, and the rest will not come back tonight. In the far corner a hole in the wall leads up and south, gnawed through old mortar. Toward the cottage hearth, you guess.

choices.text: Look at the hole in the far wall.
say: A run, gnawed through the mortar, climbing up and south. A drain. More rats may come up it.

choices.text: Look along the racks.
say: Most jars are smashed. One rack, at the north wall, is stone and not wood.

choices.text: The Oath Remembers: the stone rack.

say: The keepers kept their oil in stone. You know the pattern. You lift the lid on the north rack without a search: five flasks, sound, sealed.

choices.text: Search the racks. One turn.

say: The stone rack, at the north wall. Five flasks of lamp oil, sound and sealed.

c3.title: The Flooded Stair
text: A broad stair keeps going down where the cellar should end, step after step into water as black and still as ink in a well. Your light lies on it and does not go in. As you watch, the water creeps up one step, quietly, as if it had been waiting for you to look away.
notes: Each turn you stay, roll a d6. On 1 or 2 the lake is restless and the water rises a step.
What this room teaches. The dungeon moves. The water is a door with a timer, not a trap. It doesn't hurt you; it makes you choose: swim now, or find the way to drain it.

choices.text: Look at the water.
say: Black and still. It rises a step, then falls back. Something is feeding it. From the twelfth step down, the stair is flooded all the way to the grotto, about thirty feet of it under water.

choices.text: Think about the swim.
say: To swim it you want two rounds of held breath and a rope line tied off at the top. Without a rope: a save, or you come up in the wrong place.

choices.text: Watch the water. One turn.

say: The water creeps up one step, quietly, and holds. Then it falls back over a turn. Something controls it.

choices.text: The Archives Are Deep: what is this stair?

say: Lamp Station Nine. The water is the lock. A lock has a key, and a key has a hand: somewhere in the station a wheel turns the lake on and off.

c3-swim.title: The Flooded Stair
text: The stair goes down into the water. The far end is the grotto, thirty feet under.
notes: This is a door with a timer, not a trap. It does not hurt you. It makes you choose: swim now, or find the way to drain it.

choices.text: Tie a rope off at the top and swim down it. One turn.

say: Two rounds, holding your breath, hand over hand. The rope stays tied off behind you.

choices.text: Swim it without a line. One turn.

say: You come up where the stair comes up, lungs burning.
You come up in the wrong place and lose a turn. Back on the steps.

choices.text: Walk down the drained stair. One turn.

say: A wet slope, knee-deep at the bottom. The iron gate stands open under it.

c4.title: The Lamp Hall
text: A long hall with a niche every ten feet down both walls, and in every niche a bronze lamp, cold, its wick long since eaten. Halfway along, a slate is bolted to the wall, scored with rows of tally marks in groups of six. The far ends of the hall are out of your light. Somewhere along it, water drips with the patience of a clock.
notes: What this room teaches. Most rooms are empty, and the clock still runs. Five exits from one hall. Choose, map, and come back.

choices.text: Look at the bronze lamps.
say: Twenty, cold. 5 gp each to a tinker. Each weighs as much as 50 coins.

choices.text: Look at the slate.
say: The keepers' tally of turns. Every sixth mark is circled: they rested on the sixth. Do the same.

choices.text: Look at the grate in the floor.
say: A grate at the middle of the hall. Rats come up through it.

choices.text: Take the bronze ear-trumpet from its hook by the slate.
say: A bronze ear-trumpet. The keepers held it to a door on their rounds.

choices.text: Take the twenty bronze lamps. One turn.

say: Twenty lamps. They clink.

c5.title: The Keepers' Dormitory
text: Twelve bunks in two rows, and in four of them the sleepers have not got up for a very long time. They lie on their backs in imperial harness gone green, hands crossed over spears, and on each breastbone a small bronze plate is riveted to the bone. As your light reaches them, the plates warm to a dull glow, and one by one they sit up.
notes: Skeletons, four. AC 7 [12], spear 1d6, speed 60' (20'), morale 12. Immune to sleep. Turned on 7 or more.
What this room teaches. Undead are the station's staff, not its monsters. They are still doing their job. The rite in the study can end it for all of them.

choices.text: Look at the plates.
say: Bronze, riveted to each breastbone, stamped with a name and IX. Vane wired them into the ward current. They are cold when pried off a fallen skeleton.

choices.text: I Know How This Was Made: the rivets.

say: The rivet is soft. One tap with a hammer and it pops. You know where to put the tap: the skeletons will find you ready.

choices.text: Turn the dead (a cleric holds up a symbol).

say: The plates flare, then go dull. The dead lie back down in their bunks.
The plates glow. The dead keep coming.

choices.text: Walk among them. The rite holds.

say: The plates are cold. The dead lie still.

choices.text: Fight the skeletons.
Back out and close the door.

c5-after.title: The Dormitory, After
text: Twelve bunks in two rows. Eight are empty. The other keepers are in the shrine, or in the lake. Three footlockers stand at the bunk-feet, still shut.

choices.text: Look at the empty bunks.
say: Eight. The other keepers are in C11, or in the lake.

choices.text: Open the footlockers. One turn.

say: 140 silver in the first, 60 gold in a knotted sock in the second, a silver service medal on a ribbon in the third.

c6.title: The Ward Room
text: Eight walls, and on every wall carved eyes, dozens of them, lids wide, each with a bead of glass for a pupil. A ring of bronze is set into the floor, and in its middle a plinth holds a hooded lantern in a cradle of green-stained metal. As you step toward it, every eye in the room turns its glass a fraction, and your torch flame bows flat as if a door had opened.
notes: Any flame that is not green gutters out inside the ring. Infravision works.
What this room teaches. Light is a resource, and a site has rules. This room plants a tool before anyone explains it.

choices.text: Look at the eyes.
say: Sensor eyes and wards at once: they see heat and colour and hold what they are told to hold. The same make as in the Gorgon Queen's chamber. Hers went dark when she died. These are open.

choices.text: Look at the floor ring.
say: Bronze wires run from the ring into the walls, toward the lamp-stones and toward the pool.

choices.text: Look at the lantern on the plinth.
say: A bronze hooded lantern with a lens of green crystal, in a cradle of green-stained metal. It burns ordinary oil, 24 turns a flask. Light green, thirty feet.

choices.text: I Remember When: the lamp stations.

say: You remember lamp stations lit across the lake at night, a chain of green. The sign you were told to watch for is a green light on the isle. This lamp is it.

choices.text: Lift the lamp from its cradle. One turn.

say: Every eye in the room closes at once. The ring goes dead. The lamp is warm in your hand, and heavy.

choices.text: Break down the locked door to the south. Three turns, each loud.

say: The lock gives on the third blow. The door hangs open.

c7.title: The Lampwright's Study
text: A study, square and dry, the only room down here that still smells of paper. A man sits at the desk in a quilted robe gone the colour of tea, and he has been bones for longer than The Fort has stood. His skull rests on his folded arms as if he had laid it down to think. Before him, squared neatly, a stack of notes; at his elbow, a brass tube on a stand, aimed at a wall that is not there.
notes: Each finding takes one turn to read. The Minister reads hymn-script and can read the notes. Without her, only the Elf Minister and the Paladin read at that pace. Others need two turns a finding.
What this room teaches. Reading a site's history pays. Six turns of reading, three wandering checks, and the climax changes shape. The trade at the heart of old-school play: time for knowledge.

choices.text: Look at Ostrel Vane.
say: A bronze signet on his finger, stamped with a lamp and IX. He is not undead. He is bones in a chair, and he has been patient.

choices.text: Look at the brass tube.
say: An instrument on a stand. Through the eyepiece the water's depth and the Door's state show as rings of green light. Heavy.

choices.text: Look at the doors.

g6.title: The Drowned Landing
text: The stair comes up out of the water onto a broad, flooded shelf of rock, and the water here is warm as blood and full of slow ribbons that are not weed. To the east the shelf narrows to a ledge along a great dark pool. Out on the pool, without a sound, a wide ring spreads and fades.
notes: What this room teaches. Hazards cost time, not lives. Leeches are a toll. Salt from the cottage pays it in a round.

choices.text: Look at the ring on the pool.
say: The Warden, turning over, far out. It does not come yet. It is on the other side of the shelf, and the rim ledge east leads straight to it.

choices.text: Look at the water around your legs.
say: Slow ribbons that are not weed. Each of you has picked up 1d4 already.

choices.text: Salt or burn the leeches off. One turn.

say: Salt, or a torch held low: they drop off whole. A round each, and no blood.

choices.text: Tear them off. Each costs 1 hp.

say: They come away with a wet sound, and take a little of you with them.

g6-up.title: The Flooded Stair, Going Up
text: The stair rises west into black water. The far end is the cellar, thirty feet above.

choices.text: Swim up the rope line. One turn.

say: Hand over hand, up the rope you tied off. The cellar air is dry and cold.

choices.text: Swim up without a line. One turn.

say: You break the surface on the steps.
You come up in the wrong place and lose a turn.

choices.text: Walk up the drained stair. One turn.

g7.title: The Warden's Pool
text: The cave opens into a hall of water so wide your light can't find its far side. Far down, something glows a dim, steady green, like a coal in a deep grate. Then the glow rises.

The water bulges, slides off a back as broad as a barn door, and a head comes up: whiskers thick as ship's cable, a mouth that could take a man to the waist, and round its neck a band of green bronze set with one dark stone.
notes: The Warden. AC 4 [15], HD 8+3, bite 2d8 and four feelers 1d4, swim 90' (30'). Immune to sleep. 38 hp. Morale 8. The pool is 40 feet deep.
What this room teaches. The climax rewards what you did earlier. Every way past it comes from a choice made in another room. A party that read, watched and listened wins without a fight.

choices.text: Look at the collar.
say: A control collar of riveted bronze. The keystone at the throat is a dark stone. It glows green when the collar is working.

choices.text: Look at the bell.
say: On a bronze frame on the feeding ledge. Ringing it is loud.

choices.text: Look at the rim ledge.
say: Wet and slick, five to ten feet wide, round the south and west sides. Running on it: save or slide into the water.

choices.text: Look under the feeding ledge.
say: Ten feet down: the keepers' offerings and the Warden's leavings. Old coins.

choices.text: Ask what you know of it.
say: Say what each of you knows. The answers change the fight.

choices.text: Dive for the feeding shelf. Three turns, 300 gp a turn.

say: Nine hundred gold in old coin, in three trips down the dark.

choices.text: Raise the collar from the feeding shelf. One turn.

say: The bronze is cold and heavy. Five hundred gold, as metal.

g7-moments.title: What Each of You Knows
text: Say it before the Warden does. Each of you has one true fact to give.

choices.text: I Know How This Was Made: the collar.

say: The keystone is set in soft solder. One blow at the seam.

choices.text: I've Read About This: the collar.

say: The collar is a lock, and the keystone is its seat. Break the stone and the fish is only a fish. Sleep will not touch something this old. A bolt of force at the keystone would, when the head is up.

choices.text: The Archives Are Deep: what is the station for?

say: The station watched the door below. The Warden is its watchman. The collar answers to the station's own green light: a lamp, held up, is a keeper's face.

choices.text: The Oath Remembers: the Warden.

say: Your sense finds nothing evil in it. It is a servant, not a monster. The knights once rode here to relieve the keepers. Carry the lamp, and the oath to protect the keeper becomes an oath to protect the bearer.

choices.text: The Land Speaks: the pool.

say: The pool runs north under the isle, toward the Deep. Is the collar a tool, a wound, or a conversation? The land says: ask the fish.

choices.text: Speak with Animals: ask the Warden.

say: It is old, hungry and tired. It does not want to hurt you. It wants the collar off, and the deep water.

choices.text: I Remember When: catfish like this.

say: You have seen catfish this size in imperial harness, pulling barges. They were not wild, and they were not unhappy. You can stand on dry rock past ten feet from the edge, and it cannot reach you.

choices.text: The Minister holds up her holy symbol.
say: She holds up her lake-stone. It is the same stone as the lamp-stones. The Warden hesitates for one round.
She asks the hard question, to no one in particular: "Do we free it, or do we keep it on its chain because we are afraid of the Door?"

choices.text: Look at the pool again.

g7-arm.title: The North Arm
text: A ten-foot ledge beside deep water runs a hundred and twenty feet north to the Door. The Warden lies in the pool, and its head is turning toward the sound of you.
notes: On any dry rock, standing still, it cannot find you. In the water it attacks. On the rim ledge, moving, it lunges. Within twenty feet of the Door it attacks, moving or not, unless shown the lamp.

choices.text: Light the Warden's Lamp and show it the green light. One turn.

say: The green light lies across the water between you. The Warden sinks, and lies still beneath it. It remembers a face. It lets you pass, for as long as the lamp burns, and it fights back if attacked.

choices.text: The lamp-stone dish is lit. Walk the arm while the pool is empty. One turn.

say: The pool is empty. The Warden has gone to its post at the lit stone. You walk.

choices.text: Wait out its circuit, then cross. Three turns.

say: The swell leaves the pool and goes round the isle, clockwise. The water lies empty. You cross.

choices.text: Ring the bell with a crate of salt fish in hand, then walk. One turn.

say: The bell is loud. The Warden goes to the feeding ledge and eats, and ignores everyone not in the water. You walk.

choices.text: Stand still. Only one of you moves at a time. Two turns.

say: It hears with its skin. You stand on dry stone, and you are not there. One at a time, you cross.
It finds the one who moved.

choices.text: Ask it to hold still. Break the keystone while it does. One turn.

say: It lifts its head and holds still. The keystone shatters under the blow. The Warden thrashes for one round, then swims out through the water gate, north to the Deep, and does not come back. The lamp-stones go dark.

choices.text: Strike the seam in the solder. One turn.

say: The head comes up. One blow at the seam, and the keystone pops free. The Warden thrashes for one round, then swims out through the water gate, north to the Deep, and does not come back. The lamp-stones go dark.

choices.text: Strike the keystone when its head comes up. One turn.

say: The blow lands. Ten points, and the stone breaks. The Warden thrashes for one round, then swims out through the water gate, north to the Deep, and does not come back. The lamp-stones go dark.
The head comes up, and takes a bite at you as you strike. The stone holds.

choices.text: Fight it.
Walk the north arm to the Door.

say: You walk the rim and the arm, and nothing rises.

g8.title: The Door Beneath the Lake
text: The ledge ends in a low cave under the cliff, its far half flooded and still. Set into the north wall, across the water, is a door: a disc of black stone fifteen feet across, banded in bronze, its lower half sunk in the pool. Twelve eyes are carved round its rim, and every one of them is shut.
Beyond that wall there is only the lake, and then the Deep; the door is turned to face it, as if it expects to be knocked on from the other side.
notes: This is as far as the delve goes. The Door stays shut.
What this room teaches. Not every door is for opening. Some are for knowing about.

choices.text: Look at the Door.
say: Black stone, bronze bands, no handle, no lock, no seam you can find. Reaching it from the dry ledge means a twenty-foot swim. It faces north, toward the Deep.

choices.text: Count the eyes.
say: Twelve, all shut. The same make as the eyes in the Gorgon Queen's chamber, and the open eyes of the ward room. These are shut, waiting.

choices.text: Put your ear to the stone.
say: Very far down, the singing of the Shallows.

choices.text: Look at the stone shelf.
say: Keepers' offerings. A gold disc stamped with an open eye. And, if the Saltmen tried: a crowbar, bent, and a chalk copy of the eyes on a board. The Readers asked for it.

choices.text: The Archives Are Deep: you know this door.

say: This is the door beneath the lake. You know it on sight. The keeper in the warning may mean whoever holds the lamp. You speak first, and the others listen.

choices.text: The Land Speaks: what the rock remembers.

say: The land remembers a city where the lake is now, and remembers the water coming in. The Door is the empire's work. The rock it is cut into is older, and the land has not forgiven either.

choices.text: Take the gold disc from the shelf.

say: Four hundred gold. The Paladin says nothing, and looks at you.

choices.text: Copy the eyes onto your map. One turn.

say: Twelve eyes, each with one heavy lid. You ask yourself who else wants them open.

choices.text: Try to open the Door. One turn.
Leave it shut.

g8-try-1.title: The Door
text: The eyes twitch under their lids.

choices.text: Try again. One turn.
Leave it shut.

g8-try-2.title: The Door
text: The water in the cave rises a foot.

choices.text: Try again. One turn.
Leave it shut.

g8-try-3.title: The Door
text: Far above you, the lamp-stones hum loud enough to hear down here.

choices.text: Try again. One turn.
Leave it shut.

g8-try-4.title: The Door
text: Nothing more happens here. That night every one of you dreams of a long stair going down, north. No damage. No door.

choices.text: Leave it shut.
